findings.finding: Qualify original P06 native artifacts first, then add strict measured diagnostics before selecting an optimization. Current records already separate device-context counters, process duration, model creation, stage submit/wait/close and host bridge. Rank candidate costs without adding overlapping spans or treating simulation wall time as hardware latency.

Each three-launch model allocates three independent queues, nine device buffers and fifteen events; it also transfers the same 64-byte output weights twice. A scoped reusable model workspace could reduce lifecycle overhead, but only after baseline shows meaningful host cost. Queue reuse needs explicit sticky-error recovery and model memory-accounting changes; it is not a safe incidental refactor.

Native ManagedMatmul permits a second live operation from sequential submit calls; each creates its own Queue. Queue enqueue_mu_ is an instance member, while Device cp_mu_ protects individual command submissions only. Therefore DCR setup sequences can interleave before launch. Native docs say one caller at a time but do not forbid multiple live operations; Python separately enforces single active ownership. This is an existing native concurrency contract gap and should be retained as a bounded follow-up, not silently enabled by queue/workspace optimization.

Do not remove destination poison, collapse model output blocks, or reuse residency within the frozen baseline: those change its measured workload and trace/memory obligations. Keep exact source numerical references, stage ordering, timeout ownership, failure propagation and actual cleanup checks.

limitations: Original P06 native archives were not supplied to this assignment; no measured bottleneck ranking is asserted.
Concurrent native queue race is demonstrated by reachable code and lock scope, not fresh simulated execution.
Local native builds were intentionally not attempted under the recorded disk prerequisite shortfall.
